The app extracts supported links, checks message and address text with separate classifiers, and optionally compares addresses against OpenPhish. Email upload parses .eml content. QR upload uses OpenCV. The frontend currently does not automatically visit destinations or follow shortened links.

No match is not proof of safety. Community licensing permission must be reviewed before business deployment.

Use the current temporary public tunnel URL only while it remains active: https://elite-charity-argue-karen.trycloudflare.com. Local alternative: http://127.0.0.1:5173/. Keep the frontend, backend and tunnel running. Enable Check OpenPhish scam reports. First use an ordinary message, then a suspicious request, then a currently listed link, then a prepared QR image or .eml file. Never open listed phishing websites. If a listed link expires, choose a fresh entry. Source: output/pdf/Maso-Frontend-Test-Pack.pdf.

text:
Roadmap, not completed claims: independent held-out evaluation, broader language testing, response-time and concurrent-load measurement, improved input-specific explanations and robust hosted deployment. The <=5 second and 1,000 concurrent-user targets from the original brief have not been established. Exact brand impersonation detection and sender mismatch evidence are not fully integrated. Commercial OpenPhish licensing must be addressed before business use.
